services.heroParagraphs: Ivy Cleans is a local, insured business, and we provide cleaning and janitorial services across Houston for homes, apartments, offices, and small commercial spaces. Our team knows what nine or ten months of running air conditioning does to a house, what clay-soil mud does to an entry tile, and what Gulf humidity does to grout and caulk. We clean with all of that in mind. Ceiling fan blades, baseboards, the track under a sliding patio door, the ring at the base of a faucet — those are the spots our customers tell us they notice first when we’re done.

Our work holds up to a close look because we do it the same way on every job. We tell you what we’re cleaning before we start, we bring what we need, and a room isn’t finished until the corners match the middle. A one-bedroom apartment gets the same routine as a four-bedroom two-story with a game room over the garage. Run a finger along the top of a door frame after we leave — we’d rather you check.
Do you have a mess that needs cleaning? Is your house or office overdue for a real top-to-bottom once-over? Is there a cleaning project you keep pushing to next weekend?
Home or business, call our professional cleaning company today and ask us for a quote on the work you need done.
Pick up the phone and reach Ivy Cleans, and we’ll put together an estimate for your space.
services.serviceIntro: We handle a full range of professional cleaning work in Houston and the communities around it, from regular maid service and one-time deep cleans to move-out scrubs, apartment turnovers, and steady office upkeep for local businesses. Our house cleaners have years behind them, and they arrive with quality products and equipment matched to what they’re cleaning — sealed stone gets treated differently than laminate. Schedules here run long and odd, so we build ours around yours, weekday or weekend, weekly or once a season.

Late winter through spring, oak and pine pollen drifts in through every opened door and settles on shelves, blinds, and fan blades. The rest of the year, the air handler keeps circulating what’s already inside. Our dusting service pulls all of it off your surfaces so the air in your rooms feels clean again.

Gumbo clay turns to slick mud after every heavy rain, and it rides in on shoes, paws, and stroller wheels. Add grit from the driveway and crumbs from a summer of kids indoors dodging the heat. Our vacuuming reaches carpet, rugs, tile grout lines, and the edges along the baseboards.

Humidity here doesn’t take many days off, so bathrooms stay damp long after the shower is done, and mildew finds the grout, the caulk line, and the underside of the toilet tank. Hard water leaves its own film on glass and chrome. We scrub all of it back, cutting down germs and leaving a safe, healthy space for your family.

Between spring pollen, sideways rain off a Gulf storm, and sprinkler heads throwing mineral-heavy water across the glass, Houston windows cloud over fast. Our window cleaning clears the film and the spotting inside and out, along with the sills and tracks, and the whole house reads brighter for it.
sections.services.cards.dusting: Dusting matters more here because the air conditioning runs nearly all year, pushing fine particles through the vents and dropping them on every flat surface in the house. Add spring pollen thick enough to color a porch rail yellow, and the buildup is constant. We work top down — fan blades, shelves, blinds, door frames, baseboards — so your rooms stay easier to breathe in between visits.
sections.services.cards.vacuuming: Floors in this city take a beating from the weather. Heavy rain turns the clay yard into mud that gets tracked across entry tile, and the long hot stretch keeps everyone inside on the carpet. Our vacuuming service covers carpet, area rugs, hard floors, and the strip along the baseboards where grit collects, leaving your living space cleaner underfoot and easier to keep that way.
sections.services.cards.bathroom: Bathrooms in a humid climate rarely get a chance to dry out, and that’s how mildew takes hold in grout, along caulk seams, and behind the shower door track. Mineral-heavy water leaves its own haze on glass and fixtures. Our bathroom cleaning scrubs tile, tubs, sinks, and toilets down to the surface, knocking out bacteria and giving your family a room that’s genuinely sanitary.
sections.services.cards.window: Windows around Houston pick up a mix of pollen, storm spatter, and the chalky spray from lawn sprinklers, and a hazy summer sky doesn’t help. Our window cleaners wash the glass on both sides, wipe down the sills, and clear the tracks where dirt and dead insects gather. The result is clear glass, more daylight in your rooms, and a house that looks cared for from the curb.
sections.services.cards.upholstery: Sofas and armchairs hold on to the humidity, and along with it the pet hair, sunscreen, spilled tea, and everyday body oils that come with living indoors through a long, hot summer. Fabric near a big south-facing window fades and stiffens on top of that. Our upholstery cleaning lifts the soil out of the weave and freshens the cushions, so your seating feels and smells clean again.
sections.deep.whatIs: A deep clean covers what a regular visit doesn’t have time for: every surface wiped down, floors scrubbed out to the edges and corners, carpets and upholstery worked over, plus baseboards, vents, door frames and the tops of cabinets. It lifts out the dirt, dust and allergens an ordinary clean leaves behind. That matters here because Houston homes sit shut against the humidity most of the year, with the air conditioning pushing the same air past registers and returns, and late winter through spring coats everything in oak and pine pollen. What’s left is a healthier, more comfortable home.
sections.suburb.katy.intro: Our house cleaners work in Katy every week, and the first thing you notice out here is scale. A four or five bedroom house with three and a half baths and two staircases isn’t the exception on these streets, it’s the standard floorplan. That means longer crew hours than a smaller place needs, and it means we plan the route through your home before we start — upstairs baths and bedrooms first, main floor and hard surfaces last, so nothing gets walked back over.
sections.suburb.katy.homes: Most of what we clean here sits inside a gated, master-planned community with its own amenity center. Cinco Ranch has been going since 1991, so those brick homes are settled now — original grout in the secondary baths, real wear on stair treads, and four to five bedrooms to work through. Firethorne has been building across its 1,400 acres since 2005 and still isn’t finished, so one street is lived-in and the next is fresh drywall dust. Elyson and Cane Island are newer again, with floorplans around 2,800 square feet, big windows, and tile or luxury vinyl running through most of the ground floor. Cross Creek Ranch and Pine Mill Ranch fall somewhere in between. Newer fittings mean fewer nasty surprises and a lot more glass.
sections.suburb.katy.local: Backyard pools and lake or greenbelt frontage mean the back door is the dirtiest door in a Katy house — wet feet, cut grass, and pool water on tile, and we hit that entry and the adjoining hard floor first. All that glass in the newer builds shows every splash and every fingerprint, so it gets done properly rather than wiped. Late January brings the damp, foggy mornings that spike mold counts here, which is when shower glass, caulk lines and window tracks need the shorter scrub cycle. February through April, oak pollen puts a yellow film on sills, entry floors and ceiling fan blades. The air conditioning runs nearly all year, so we take the supply and return registers too.
sections.suburb.sugar-land.intro: We clean homes all over Sugar Land, from two-bath townhomes to five-bedroom houses on golf-course lots. The thing that shapes nearly every job here is that the air never dries out. Shower glass films over, grout darkens along the same three lines, and window tracks stay damp days after a rain. So we scrub bathrooms on a shorter cycle than a crew in a dry climate would plan for, and we open the doors that stay closed — closets, pantries, the cabinet under the sink — because that’s where the moisture sits.
sections.suburb.sugar-land.homes: First Colony isn’t one neighborhood so much as an umbrella over sixty-plus subdivisions, close to 14,000 houses plus townhomes and condos, which means we might clean a compact two-bath unit in the morning and a two-story with a back stair and a game room that afternoon. Streets in Sugar Creek and New Territory are older: original tile grout, tubs with caulk that’s been painted over more than once, ceiling fans in every bedroom. Telfair and Riverstone run newer — open plans, tall windows above the front door, wood-look plank carrying from kitchen through living room, and quartz that shows every water spot. Sweetwater’s roughly 570 households add square footage and formal rooms nobody sits in that still collect dust all the same.
sections.suburb.sugar-land.local: Homes fronting the course in Sweetwater get clippings and turf chemical residue walked in at the back door, so entry mats, the first stretch of hard floor and the mudroom baseboards get real scrubbing instead of a quick pass. From there it’s the damp. Grout, caulk lines and shower glass discolor faster here than owners expect, and closets and under-sink cabinets hold moisture twelve months a year. Late January, with fog most mornings, is a mold peak rather than a quiet stretch, and we work it that way. February through April, oak lays a yellow film on sills, blinds, fan blades and entry tile. The air conditioning barely stops, so registers and the ceiling around them gray over and we wipe them down.
sections.suburb.pearland.intro: Ivy Cleans works Pearland houses every week, and a lot of what we do here is set by water. Shadow Creek Ranch spreads across 3,500 acres on a lake theme, and with canals sitting that close to the slab, humidity comes in the back door with everybody. Grout and window tracks show it first. We also clean for households working shifts at the Texas Medical Center about ten miles up the road, which usually means keyed or coded access and a schedule built around somebody sleeping.
sections.suburb.pearland.homes: Nearly every street here sits inside a planned community with HOA standards. Shadow Creek Ranch runs 3,500 acres on a lake theme, built out by production builders — Perry, Meritage, Coventry, Westin, Ashton Woods, D.R. Horton — so floorplans repeat down the block: two-story entry, tile through the wet rooms and traffic paths, carpet upstairs, ceiling fans in every bedroom and a garden tub nobody uses but everyone wants clean. Once our crew learns one of those plans, we can quote the next one accurately. Silverlake and Silvercreek homes are further along, with builder-grade caulk and grout that have taken two decades of humidity. Green Tee Terrace is older still, smaller rooms, mature trees over the roof. Southern Trails and City Park sit somewhere in between.
sections.suburb.pearland.local: The canals and lakes threaded through Shadow Creek Ranch keep standing water within a few yards of the slab, so bathrooms in these houses never quite dry out; shower glass, grout and caulk lines discolor faster here than owners expect, and we scrub them on a shorter cycle than we would in a dry climate. Closets and under-sink cabinets hold the same damp. Late January is the mold peak in southeast Texas, not summer, so winter visits get the window tracks and the corners behind closed doors. February through April, oak pollen lays a yellow film on sills, entry tile and fan blades. The air conditioning barely stops all year, which keeps supply vents and the ceiling around them dirty, and we can add those to a visit.
sections.suburb.the-woodlands.intro: Our team cleans homes in The Woodlands, and the tree canopy sets the terms of the job. Shade that keeps a back patio comfortable in August also keeps the north side of a house damp, so thresholds, window tracks and baseboards on that side need more attention than the sunny side of the same house. Folks here tell us their village before anything else, and that tells us plenty about the age of the fittings we’ll be scrubbing.
sections.suburb.the-woodlands.homes: Grogan’s Mill dates to 1974 and holds more than 12,000 residents now, and those streets show it: smaller, separated rooms, original bathrooms with grout that has soaked up half a century of humidity, and light fixtures hung over stairwells nobody reaches without a ladder. Panther Creek and Cochran’s Crossing sit in the middle, where remodels mean one bathroom is new and the other still has the original cultured marble. Creekside Park and College Park are the newer builds — open kitchens running into two-story family rooms, wood-look tile across the whole first floor, tall entry windows, and counters that show every drip. Sterling Ridge and Alden Bridge land between the two. We size the visit off the house, not the square footage on paper.
sections.suburb.the-woodlands.local: Leaf litter is the constant here. With trails running off the back of so many streets, oak and pine debris rides in on shoes and grinds into entry tile and stair treads, so entries and hard floors come first on our way through a house. Shaded patios and north-facing rooms stay damp, so we scrub shower glass, caulk lines and window tracks on a shorter cycle than owners expect. Late January is a mold peak in southeast Texas rather than a quiet stretch, so closets and under-sink cabinets get opened and wiped in winter. From February into April oak pollen lays a yellow film on sills, blinds and fan blades, and vents and registers collect it all year with the air conditioning running.
sections.suburb.missouri-city.intro: Our cleaners work Missouri City every week, from the lakeside blocks in Lakes of Brightwater to the First Colony streets that fall on this side of the city line. What shapes the job here is that there’s no off month. The humidity holds all twelve, the air conditioning barely rests, and something is always in the air — cedar in January, oak through the spring, Bermuda grass hanging on into October. Dust, film on the sills and mildew in the bathrooms all come back on a schedule, so we clean on one too.
sections.suburb.missouri-city.homes: Most of what we clean here is planned-community housing on curving streets, and the floor plans repeat in ways our crews know by heart: a tiled entry, carpet up the stair run, and a kitchen open to the family room, which leaves one unbroken run of hard floor from the front door to the back patio with no natural place to stop mopping. In Lakes of Brightwater the water is close, so shoes track in damp and the entry tile and grout show it first. The First Colony sections inside Missouri City tend to run larger — more bathrooms, more glass shower doors, more ceiling fans sitting high over a two-story living room. Older streets bring older fittings, where caulk lines and shower tracks need patience rather than pressure.
sections.suburb.missouri-city.local: There’s no dry season here and winter lows barely touch freezing, so the soil load never resets. Grout, caulk, shower glass and window tracks in Missouri City bathrooms discolor faster than owners expect, and we scrub them on a shorter cycle than a crew in a dry climate ever would. Late January is the mold peak in southeast Texas, pushed by damp, foggy mornings, so we go hardest at closets, under-sink cabinets and back bedrooms in the weeks people assume are the quiet ones. February through April, oak lays a yellow film on sills, blinds, entry floors and fan blades; grass pollen takes over and carries it into fall. Vents and registers gray up from air conditioning that never really stops, and we’ll wipe those and the ceiling around them when you ask.
sections.suburb.memorial.intro: We clean homes in Memorial, from the condos and townhomes stacked around CityCentre to the established houses on the streets behind them. The one condition that shapes nearly every job here is air that never dries out. Warm, damp months run straight into each other with no real break, so shower glass clouds over, grout darkens and window tracks build a film faster than most owners expect. We put those surfaces on a shorter scrubbing cycle than a crew in a dry climate ever would.
sections.suburb.memorial.homes: The Memorial Corridor has been filling in with residential building for years, and CityCentre sits in the middle of that shift: newer condos and townhomes with compact floor plans, hard flooring wall to wall, frameless shower glass, stone counters and tall windows that show every smudge and every water spot. Those units clean quickly but forgive nothing. Step off the corridor and the established housing is a different job altogether, with more square footage, more bathrooms, tile floors whose grout has been down long enough to hold color, fans turning on high ceilings, and baseboards and built-ins that want a hand and a cloth instead of a mop. We staff and time the two kinds of homes differently.
sections.suburb.memorial.local: The split between the newer CityCentre units and the older houses behind the corridor decides where the trouble collects. In a compact condo it’s the interior bathroom with no window, where caulk lines, shower glass and the tracks under sliding doors gray over fast, so we scrub them every visit rather than now and then. In the larger established homes it’s closets, under-sink cabinets and any room kept shut. Late January is the mold peak here, not August, so winter is when we push hardest on grout and cabinet interiors. Air conditioning runs almost twelve months and dirties supply vents, registers and the ceiling around them. Oak pollen films sills, entry floors and fan blades from February into April, and we lift that dust out instead of moving it around.

findings:
I'll research this market systematically. Let me start with searches on Houston suburbs, neighborhoods, and climate.Good foundation. Now let me research subdivisions per area and housing stock details.I ran seven web searches before the search tool hit its usage limit for this session. Below is everything the pages actually supported. **Two of the five sections — (d) ZIP codes and (e) keywords — I could not research at all, and I have deliberately left them empty rather than reconstruct them from memory.** Several areas also came back with no verifiable subdivision names; those are flagged as such.

Sources used: click2houston.com, brookfieldresidential.com, texasrealestatesource.com, extraspace.com, houstonproperties.com, compass.com, har.com, sugarlandtxhome.com, vantagerec.com, txpremiermortgage.com, thewoodlands.guide, houstonmethodist.org, mcgovernallergy.com, abc13.com, pollen.day, en.wikipedia.org.

---

**Suburbs / separate cities**

| Area | Position relative to Houston | Source support |

| **Sugar Land** | Southwest of Houston | Brookfield Residential |
| **Pearland** | 15 miles south of downtown along Highway 288 | texasrealestatesource |
| **The Woodlands** | About 28 miles north of Houston | Brookfield Residential |
| **League City** | Southeast, on Galveston Bay with boating and beach access | texasrealestatesource |
| **Missouri City** | Southwest, adjacent to Sugar Land — the First Colony community overlaps into it | vantagerec, har.com |
| **Fulshear** | West/far-west, described as the "country living" end of the metro | texasrealestatesource |

**Neighborhoods inside the City of Houston**

| Area | Position | Source support |
|---|---|---|

*Deliberately excluded as sub-parts, not peers:* Cinco Ranch (inside Katy), First Colony and Telfair (inside Sugar Land), Shadow Creek Ranch (inside Pearland), Alden Bridge and the other villages (inside The Woodlands), Rice Military, Upper Kirby, Tanglewood, Museum District, Eastwood and Midtown appeared in results as Houston neighborhoods and are legitimate candidates, but I did not get enough on them to write pages and left them off rather than pad the list.

---

## (b) SUBDIVISIONS AND DEVELOPMENTS

**Katy** — verified: **Cinco Ranch**, **Cane Island**, **Firethorne**, **Pine Mill Ranch** (click2houston); **Elyson** (Brookfield, har.com, texasrealestatesource); **Cross Creek Ranch** (texasrealestatesource, described as a Katy-area community). Cinco Ranch is the largest residential development in the Katy area, sitting on both sides of the Grand Parkway south of I-10, almost entirely in Fort Bend County. HAR lists 50 subdivisions *within* Cinco Ranch alone.

**Sugar Land** — verified: **First Colony**, **Sweetwater** / **Sweetwater Estates**, **Telfair**, **Riverstone**, **New Territory**, **Sugar Creek**, **Commonwealth** (which itself contains **Sutton Forest**, **Sutton Park** and **Oxford**), and **Avalon** (sugarlandtxhome, har.com, vantagerec, byjoandco). First Colony is an umbrella master plan with more than 61 subdivisions under it.

**Pearland** — verified: **Shadow Creek Ranch**, **Silverlake** (also written Silver Lake), **Silvercreek**, **Southern Trails**, **Green Tee Terrace**, **City Park** (houstonproperties, har.com, Wikipedia). Shadow Creek Ranch is west of SH-288 and south of Beltway 8. Note: **Pomona** and **Sedona Lakes** turned up on the same page but are in **Manvel**, not Pearland — don't file them under Pearland.

**The Woodlands** — verified, and the local vocabulary is "villages," not subdivisions: **Grogan's Mill**, **Panther Creek**, **Cochran's Crossing**, **Indian Springs**, **Alden Bridge**, **Sterling Ridge**, **College Park**, **Creekside Park**, **Carlton Woods**, plus **Town Center** (txpremiermortgage, sharonhartrealty, thewoodlandsrelocationguide, thewoodlands.guide). Nine residential villages in total. (Note: the two "village order" sources disagree on which village opened first, so don't publish founding order.)

**Missouri City** — only one verified name: **Lakes of Brightwater** (har.com), plus the portion of **First Colony** that overlaps the city. Thin — needs another pass before it gets a page.

**River Oaks** — **no subdivision names verified.** Compass listed "Avalon Place" and "Briar Hollow" as adjacent search areas, not as subdivisions inside River Oaks, so I am not reporting them as such.

**The Heights, Montrose, Memorial, League City, Fulshear** — **no subdivision or sub-neighborhood names verified.** For The Heights I saw the neighborhood named only as a whole; for Memorial I found only **CityCentre**, which the source describes as a mixed-use development, not a residential subdivision. These five areas need a dedicated search round before any development names go on a website.

---

## (c) HOUSING AND LOCAL CONDITIONS

### Houston as a whole

**Climate.** Houston is subtropical, with most of Greater Houston in USDA plant hardiness zone 9 — long, hot, often muggy summers and mild winter lows that barely fall below freezing (Houston Methodist). There is no hard freeze season and no dry season to speak of.

**Humidity and mold — the single biggest cleaning driver.** The Houston Methodist allergist quoted describes the humid environment as making Houston "a hotspot for dust mite and mold allergens," and calls them perennial, year-round allergens. McGovern Allergy adds that high humidity, frequent rainfall and warm temperatures let mold thrive, that it grows in hidden places rather than only obvious ones, and that air conditioners themselves can harbor mold without regular maintenance; they recommend holding indoor humidity at 30–50%. ABC13 reported mold spore counts across southeast Texas hitting the extreme category at the end of January, driven by damp, foggy mornings — i.e. mold peaks in *winter* here, not summer.

> **What it means for cleaning:** bathrooms never fully dry out, so grout, caulk lines, shower glass and window tracks discolour faster than owners expect and need scrubbing on a shorter cycle than in a dry climate. Closets, under-sink cabinets and any room behind a closed door hold moisture. Dust-mite load in soft surfaces is a year-round problem, not seasonal — mattresses, upholstery and drapes matter more here. Because AC runs nearly all year and the units themselves can hold mold, supply and return vents, registers and the surrounding ceiling get visibly dirty and are worth listing as an add-on. Winter is not a slow, clean season in Houston — late January is a mold peak.

**Pollen.** Houston's season runs nearly the whole year (pollen.day). Tree pollen starts as early as December; mountain cedar drives "cedar fever" in January; oak, pine, ash, elm, pecan and mulberry peak February through April, and oak alone can visibly blanket the city in yellow. Grass pollen — Bermuda, Johnson, Bahia, ryegrass — takes over from late April through summer into early fall, with Bermuda producing symptoms into October. Alternaria and Cladosporium moulds run year-round alongside dust mites and urban ozone.

> **What it means for cleaning:** February–April is the visible-yellow-film season on sills, entry floors, ceiling fans and anything near a door. Allergy-driven demand is real and it is not confined to spring — sell recurring service on the basis that there is no month without an airborne load.

**Not found — do not publish these.** I found **nothing** in these searches on: typical Houston foundation type (slab-on-grade is widely assumed but I did not verify it), typical flooring, the age and construction of the city's general housing stock, hard-water/mineral-scale conditions, or coastal salt air. All of that is genuinely useful copy and all of it needs its own search round. Road salt, desert dust, blowing sand and wildfire smoke did not appear in any result and I would not expect them to apply here.

### Area by area

**Katy.** Cinco Ranch opened in 1991 and has held its appeal for 30-plus years; most homes there have four to five bedrooms and brick construction is the norm (texasrealestatesource). Elyson is a 3,600-acre development of roughly 1,500 new-construction homes around private lakes and greenbelts, with typical floorplans around 2,800 sq ft and lots big enough for backyard pools. Firethorne has been building since 2005 with construction still ongoing, on 1,400 acres with 150 acres of parks and lakes. → *Large, HOA-governed, gate-and-amenity communities; 2,800 sq ft and up with four to five bedrooms means multi-bathroom, multi-storey jobs and longer crew hours. Backyard pools and lake/greenbelt frontage mean tracked-in grass and pool water at back doors. Newer stock means fewer deferred-maintenance surprises but more glass and more hard-surface floor.*

**Sugar Land.** First Colony spans 9,700 acres with over 60,000 residents and nearly 14,000 homes, 1,700 apartments, 750 townhomes and 169 condos, across 61-plus subdivisions (vantagerec). Sweetwater is an upscale golf-course neighborhood of roughly 570 households, built around Sweetwater Country Club, and belongs to the First Colony HOA with its ten pools (sugarlandtxhome). Telfair is one of Sugar Land's newest neighborhoods with 250-plus acres of parks and lakes. → *A single HOA umbrella covering tens of thousands of homes is a referral network — one satisfied street in First Colony reaches a lot of similar households. Housing type ranges from condo and townhome to golf-course estate, so quote ranges have to be wide. Golf-course frontage means turf chemicals and clippings at entryways.*

**Pearland.** Most residential areas sit inside planned communities governed by HOAs that maintain neighborhood standards (houstonproperties). Shadow Creek Ranch covers 3,500 acres on a lake theme, roughly 10 miles from the Texas Medical Center, and was built out by a long roster of production builders including Perry, Meritage, Coventry, Westin, Ashton Woods and D.R. Horton (har.com, Wikipedia). → *Production-builder stock means repeating floorplans — a crew that learns one Shadow Creek plan can price the next one accurately. The lake-and-canal layout across 3,500 acres adds standing water and humidity right at the property line. Proximity to the Medical Center points at shift-working medical households, which favours keyed/coded access and flexible scheduling.*

**The Woodlands.** Nine villages of very different ages: Grogan's Mill was founded in 1974 and now holds over 12,000 residents, while College Park and Creekside Park are among the newer sections (txpremiermortgage). The area is known for heavy tree cover, parks and nature trails (Brookfield). → *Age spread matters — a 1970s Grogan's Mill house and a Creekside Park house are different cleaning jobs. The defining local condition is the tree canopy: dense shade keeps exteriors, patios and north-facing rooms damp, and leaf litter and pollen come in on shoes from the trail network. Sell the villages by name; residents identify by village, not by "The Woodlands."*

**River Oaks.** Described as Houston's first master-planned community, spanning more than 1,100 acres, built around River Oaks Boulevard and the country club, with oversized traditional American homes by architects including John Staub and Birdsall P. Briscoe, alongside gated condos and townhouses (houstonproperties, cubesmart, diggz). → *Large historic estates with period detail — this is detail-cleaning work, not square-footage work: original millwork, stone, wood floors and antique surfaces that need specified products. Expect gated access and staff coordination. The mature oak canopy the neighborhood is named for drops constant leaf and pollen litter.*

**The Heights.** One of Houston's oldest neighborhoods (diggz); demand and prices for homes there and in Montrose are consistently rising (cubesmart). → *Old inner-Loop housing implies renovation dust, original wood floors and small-lot street parking — but I did not verify the era, size or construction of Heights housing, so nothing more specific should be written yet.*

**Montrose.** Inner Loop, high-demand, mixed housing described only in general terms in what I found. → *Insufficient verified detail for area-specific copy.*

**Memorial.** The Memorial Corridor is on the west side and has been redeveloping toward more residential use, with CityCentre producing a range of new residential options (cubesmart). → *Suggests a newer condo/townhome component alongside established housing, but the established housing itself was not described in any result I got.*

**League City.** Waterfront living with boating, fishing and beach access on Galveston Bay (texasrealestatesource). → *Bay-front and boat-owning households mean salt exposure on glass and exterior surfaces and sand tracked indoors — though note the coastal-salt-air point is my inference from the waterfront description, not something a source stated. Verify before it goes on a page.*

**Missouri City / Fulshear.** Fulshear is characterised only as the "country living" end of the metro. Neither area produced housing-stock detail. → *No area-specific conditions verified.*

### Background only — never for the website

US News 2025–2026 rankings placed Pearland #3 and League City #6 in the US (texasrealestatesource). Most Houston suburbs show median home prices between $300K and $600K, with the range running from the $200s to over $2 million; Cinco Ranch homes list from the $400s to the $800s with some above $1–2 million (texasrealestatesource). One older roundup cites a Katy median of $208,700 (extraspace) — that conflicts with the figures above and looks stale. Pearland's combined property tax rate is about 2.13%; Katy-area community rates were quoted at 2.71%–3.54% (houstonproperties, har.com). This says the market can carry recurring residential service at professional rates across all eleven areas. **I found no flood, crime or poverty data in these searches.**

---

## (d) ZIP CODES — NOT DELIVERED

**I could not research this and am not supplying it.** My search budget was exhausted before I could reach an authoritative postal or municipal listing, and Houston ZIP codes are exactly the kind of item that looks plausible when invented and is wrong. The only ZIP that appeared anywhere in my results was **77584**, cited repeatedly as Shadow Creek Ranch — and that is **Pearland, not the City of Houston**, so it does not belong in a Houston list.

This needs one clean search against a USPS or City of Houston source, filtering out PO-box-only and non-residential codes.

## (e) KEYWORDS — NOT DELIVERED

**I ran no searches on this and have nothing sourced to report.** I could write out the obvious families — house cleaning, maid service, deep cleaning, move-out cleaning — but the whole point of the item is to capture the *local* phrasing that actually shows up in Houston search results and competitor page titles, and I have no evidence of what that is. Guessing here would defeat the purpose.

suburbs.name: Katy
suburbs.housingCharacter: Large HOA-governed master-planned communities: Cinco Ranch opened in 1991 with most homes having four to five bedrooms and brick construction the norm; Elyson is a 3,600-acre development of roughly 1,500 new-construction homes with typical floorplans around 2,800 sq ft, and Firethorne has been building since 2005 on 1,400 acres with construction still ongoing.

conditions.condition: Homes of 2,800 sq ft and up with four to five bedrooms in gate-and-amenity communities
conditions.implication: Multi-bathroom, multi-storey jobs that require longer crew hours

conditions.condition: Backyard pools and lake/greenbelt frontage
conditions.implication: Tracked-in grass and pool water at back doors

conditions.condition: Newer housing stock with lots of glass and hard-surface floor
conditions.implication: Fewer deferred-maintenance surprises but more glass and hard floor to clean

suburbs.name: Sugar Land
suburbs.housingCharacter: First Colony is an umbrella master plan spanning 9,700 acres with over 60,000 residents and nearly 14,000 homes, 1,700 apartments, 750 townhomes and 169 condos across 61-plus subdivisions; Sweetwater is an upscale golf-course neighborhood of roughly 570 households built around Sweetwater Country Club, and Telfair is one of Sugar Land's newest neighborhoods with 250-plus acres of parks and lakes.

conditions.condition: A single HOA umbrella covering tens of thousands of similar households
conditions.implication: Strong referral network — one satisfied street in First Colony reaches many comparable homes

conditions.condition: Housing ranges from condo and townhome to golf-course estate
conditions.implication: Quote ranges have to be wide to cover the spread of home types

conditions.condition: Golf-course frontage
conditions.implication: Turf chemicals and clippings tracked in at entryways

suburbs.name: Pearland
suburbs.housingCharacter: Most residential areas sit inside planned communities governed by HOAs that maintain neighborhood standards; Shadow Creek Ranch covers 3,500 acres on a lake theme and was built out by production builders including Perry, Meritage, Coventry, Westin, Ashton Woods and D.R. Horton.

conditions.condition: Production-builder stock with repeating floorplans
conditions.implication: A crew that learns one Shadow Creek plan can price the next one accurately

conditions.condition: Lake-and-canal layout across 3,500 acres
conditions.implication: Standing water and added humidity right at the property line

conditions.condition: Roughly 10 miles from the Texas Medical Center, with shift-working medical households
conditions.implication: Favours keyed or coded access and flexible scheduling

suburbs.name: The Woodlands
suburbs.housingCharacter: Nine residential villages of very different ages — Grogan's Mill was founded in 1974 and now holds over 12,000 residents, while College Park and Creekside Park are among the newer sections. The area is known for heavy tree cover, parks and nature trails.

conditions.condition: Wide age spread between villages
conditions.implication: A 1970s Grogan's Mill house and a Creekside Park house are different cleaning jobs

conditions.condition: Dense tree canopy and shade
conditions.implication: Exteriors, patios and north-facing rooms stay damp

conditions.condition: Extensive trail network and leaf litter
conditions.implication: Leaf litter and pollen come in on shoes

conditions.condition: Residents identify by village, not by "The Woodlands"
conditions.implication: Sell and market the villages by name

suburbs.name: Missouri City
suburbs.housingCharacter: Southwest of Houston and adjacent to Sugar Land, with the First Colony community overlapping into the city; no further housing-stock detail was verified.

suburbs.name: Memorial
suburbs.housingCharacter: The Memorial Corridor on the west side has been redeveloping toward more residential use, with CityCentre — a mixed-use development — producing a range of new residential options; the established housing itself was not described.

conditions.condition: A newer condo and townhome component alongside established housing
conditions.implication: Mixed job types between compact new units and older established homes

conditions.condition: Subtropical climate, with most of Greater Houston in USDA plant hardiness zone 9 — long, hot, muggy summers and mild winter lows barely below freezing, with no hard freeze season and no dry season
conditions.implication: No seasonal break in soil load; cleaning demand and moisture conditions run all twelve months

conditions.condition: High humidity makes Houston a hotspot for dust mite and mold allergens, which are perennial and year-round; high humidity, frequent rainfall and warm temperatures let mold thrive in hidden places, and indoor humidity is best held at 30–50%
conditions.implication: Bathrooms never fully dry out, so grout, caulk lines, shower glass and window tracks discolour faster than owners expect and need scrubbing on a shorter cycle than in a dry climate; closets, under-sink cabinets and any room behind a closed door hold moisture; dust-mite load in mattresses, upholstery and drapes is a year-round problem

conditions.condition: Air conditioning runs nearly all year and the units themselves can harbor mold without regular maintenance
conditions.implication: Supply and return vents, registers and the surrounding ceiling get visibly dirty and are worth listing as an add-on service

conditions.condition: Mold spore counts across southeast Texas hit the extreme category at the end of January, driven by damp, foggy mornings — mold peaks in winter here, not summer
conditions.implication: Winter is not a slow, clean season in Houston; late January is a mold peak and should be worked accordingly

conditions.condition: Pollen season runs nearly the whole year: tree pollen starts as early as December, mountain cedar drives cedar fever in January, oak, pine, ash, elm, pecan and mulberry peak February through April with oak visibly blanketing the city in yellow, and grass pollen — Bermuda, Johnson, Bahia, ryegrass — takes over from late April through summer into early fall, with Bermuda producing symptoms into October
conditions.implication: February–April is the visible-yellow-film season on sills, entry floors, ceiling fans and anything near a door; sell recurring service on the basis that there is no month without an airborne load

conditions.condition: Alternaria and Cladosporium moulds run year-round alongside dust mites and urban ozone
conditions.implication: Allergy-driven demand is real and is not confined to spring, supporting year-round recurring plans
